You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: TSMC 2026 Q2 Earnings Highlights: Revenue Hits Record High of US$40.2 Billion, Beating Expectations; Gross Margin 67.7% and Operating Margin 60.3% Both Reach All-Time Highs; Advanced Technology Mix Hits 77% Driven by Strong AI Demand

TEXT:
1. Core View
TSMC ’s 2026 Q2 earnings were robust. Consolidated revenue reached a record NT$1,270.38 billion (approximately US$40.2 billion), up 12.0% QoQ and 36.0% YoY (USD revenue up 33.7% YoY), clearly exceeding the high end of the company’s prior guidance (US$39.0–40.2 billion). Gross margin of 67.7% and operating margin of 60.3% both hit all- time highs and substantially beat market expectations (market consensus gross margin was 67.1%). Net income came in at NT$706.56 billion, up 77.4% YoY, while EPS reached NT$27.25, also up 77.4% YoY. Growth was primarily driven by strong global AI chip demand, full utilization of advanced-node capacity, and an optimized product mix. Advanced technology contribution rose to a new high of 77% (with N2 contributing 3% for the first time). Momentum accelerated in Q2 (revenue +12%, net income +23.4% vs. Q1). Market reaction was positive, and full Q3 guidance was released concurrently.
2. Detailed Breakdown
1. Overall Revenue and Profit Performance
Consolidated revenue: NT$1,270.38 billion (US$40.20 billion), +12.0% QoQ / +36.0% YoY (USD revenue +33.7% YoY / +12.0% QoQ); all-time quarterly high, above the high end of guidance.
Net income: NT$706.56 billion, +77.4% YoY / +23.4% QoQ.
EPS: NT$27.25 (approx. US$4.31 per ADR), +77.4% YoY / +23.4% QoQ.
Record margins:
Gross margin 67.7% (all-time high, well above Q1’s 66.2% and market estimate of 67.1%).
Operating margin 60.3% (all-time high, well above Q1’s 58.1%).
Net profit margin 55.6%.
vs. Expectations & Prior Quarter: USD revenue clearly exceeded both the midpoint and high end of guidance; Q2 vs. Q1 showed accelerating momentum (+12% revenue, +23.4% net income).
Key Drivers: Strong global AI chip demand, full advanced-node capacity utilization, and improved product mix.
2. Advanced Process Technology Performance (Wafer Revenue by Node)
Advanced technologies (7nm and below) expanded to 77% of total wafer revenue (new high, vs. 74% in Q1).
Breakdown:
2nm (N2): 3% (first meaningful contribution; early production ramp from 0% in Q1, indicating solid yield and customer adoption progress).
3nm: 30% (vs. ~25% in Q1).
5nm: 33% (vs. ~36% in Q1).
7nm: 11%.
Key Drivers: Continued strong demand from Apple , Nvidia , AMD and others for 3nm/2nm and CoWoS advanced packaging; HPC/AI mix continued to rise.
3. Other Business Segments
Core business remains pure-play foundry, dominated by advanced nodes (77%).
Monthly & H1 Update: June single-month revenue NT$442.68 billion (+6.2% MoM / +67.9% YoY, all-time high), which lifted Q2 above the high end of guidance; H1 cumulative revenue NT$2.404 trillion (+35.6% YoY).
Overall Momentum: Sustained strong AI/HPC demand supporting accelerating revenue and profit growth.
4. Capital Expenditure and Future Plans
Full details on CapEx plans, overseas fab (U.S./Europe/Japan) allocation, N2 yield/production progress, CoWoS expansion speed, and advanced-node pricing strategy will be provided at today’s earnings call (Taiwan time 14:00–15:30).
Five key market focus areas:
N2 (2nm) production ramp and yield.
CoWoS advanced packaging expansion speed (still an AI bottleneck).
Magnitude of full-year revenue guidance raise (previously raised to “USD revenue growth >30%”; market expects further upside).
Overseas fab CapEx allocation and margin dilution impact.
Advanced-node pricing strategy (AI premium continues).
Current available info: 2026 CapEx plan approaching a record ~US$56 billion (high end of previous US$52–56 billion guidance). AI pricing and high utilization are expected to support elevated margins, despite dilution pressure from N2 ramp and overseas fabs.
5. Next-Quarter Guidance (2026 Q3)
Official guidance already released:
Revenue: US$44.6–45.8 billion (midpoint ~US$45.2 billion, ~+12.4% QoQ).
Gross margin: 65.0%–67.0%.
Operating margin: 56.0%–58.0%.
Exchange-rate assumption: USD/NTD 32.0.
Market Consensus: Foreign brokers generally expect further upside to full-year revenue/EPS guidance. While N2 ramp and overseas fabs create some margin dilution pressure, AI pricing power and high utilization are expected to keep margins at elevated levels.
6. Market Backdrop and Investor Concerns
Core Highlights: Revenue, profit, gross margin, and advanced-node mix all hit all-time highs and beat expectations, with accelerating AI-driven momentum.
Market Challenges & Investor Focus: Early-stage N2 yield, CoWoS expansion bottlenecks, overseas-fab CapEx margin dilution, magnitude of full-year guidance raise, and sustainability of AI pricing premium.
Investor Reaction: Data comprehensively beat expectations; market reaction positive. Today’s earnings call is the next key catalyst.
